subject: Sabry et al. (1997)
object: Sabry et al. (1997) described 3 Bedouin sibs with congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I who also had dysmorphic features. These included growth retardation/short stature, congenital ptosis, abnormal tarsal bones, metatarsal duplication/hypoplasia, nail and phalangeal hypoplasia of fingers and toes, Madelung deformity, syndactyly of toes, and hallux valgus. The phenotype varied among the sibs.

subject: Sabry et al. (1997)
object: Sabry et al. (1997) found a very low mitotic index in peripheral blood lymphocyte cultures from the 3 affected sibs. They suggested that a low mitotic index and congenital ptosis could be part of the syndrome.

subject: Sabry et al. (1997)
object: Sabry et al. (1997) concluded that their report confirmed an association between a subset of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I and a specific form of distal limb anomalies. This suggested a distinct entity.

subject: Ahmed et al. (2006)
object: Ahmed et al. (2006) reported evidence of genetic heterogeneity in congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I.

subject: Ahmed et al. (2006)
object: Ahmed et al. (2006) performed linkage and mutation analysis of the CDAN1 gene in congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I and found genetic heterogeneity.

subject: Babbs et al. (2013)
object: In a consanguineous family of Middle Eastern origin with congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I, Babbs et al. (2013) used whole genome sequencing and segregation analysis to identify a homozygous c.533T>A transversion in the C15ORF41 gene, which was predicted to result in a p.L178Q substitution. No likely pathogenic CDAN1 mutation had been found in this family.

subject: Babbs et al. (2013)
object: By sequencing C15ORF41 in other congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I families without CDAN1 mutations, Babbs et al. (2013) found a homozygous c.281A>G transition, predicted to result in a p.Y94C substitution, in 2 more families of Southeast Asian origin.

subject: Babbs et al. (2013)
object: Babbs et al. (2013) reported that the haplotype around the c.281A>G mutation in C15ORF41 suggested a founder effect for this mutation in Pakistan.

subject: Babbs et al. (2013)
object: Babbs et al. (2013) noted that CDAN1 mutations underlie most cases of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I. However, no likely pathogenic CDAN1 mutation is found in about 20% of cases, which suggested that at least one other locus exists.

subject: Babbs et al. (2013)
object: Using detailed sequence similarity searches, Babbs et al. (2013) predicted that C15ORF41 encodes a novel restriction endonuclease belonging to the Holliday junction resolvase protein family.
